rv.q: With Rope, they have another audacious, stylish, and captivating production.
This incarnation of Rope is a spellbinding and thoughtful entertainment.
With a starry cast, Rope gives new life to the classic murder mystery that inspired Hitchcock's film.
And, try as it might, with a top-notch design team and a solid cast, the New Group production is neither as urbane nor as suspenseful as it wants to be.
In the end, Greenberg deserves credit for trying to unearth the subtexts buried in previous versions, but without real dramatic tension to hold it all together, this Rope goes slack.
Disappointingly, the tension among the story’s several cat-and-mouse games never grows sufficiently taut to grip one’s attention.
Greenberg has taken his Rope out of its closet only to bury it in a big wooden chest.
But this New Group production, under the direction of Scott Elliott, never achieves the compelling creepiness of the material's previous iterations.
But my frustrations with this production are best summed up by saying, “Skip Rope.”
“Rope” represents off-Broadway at its best and for that we can grade it on a curve.
The brittle repartee – reminiscent of smart scripts penned in a wittier age – is thoroughly entertaining.

cn.t: Mixed reviews for this queerer, bloodier adaptation of Hamilton's thriller, with critics praising its bold homoerotic reimagining but finding it lacks the suspense and sophistication of Hitchcock's film.
